Proton Pump Inhibitors: Mechanism of Action, Therapeutic Uses & Adverse Effects

Mechanism of Action

PPIs decrease acid secretion in the stomach by inhibiting the H/K ATPase (the proton pump) in the parietal cells

Meaning they inhibit the final step of acid secretion and that is why they have the highest efficacy in suppressing acid secretion

Proton Pump Inhibitors

FDA approved PPIs include:

  • Omeprazole
  • Esomeprazole
  • Lansoprazole
  • Dexlansoprazole
  • Pantoprazole
  • Rabeprazole

Therapeutic Uses

PPIs are used as a first line for treatment of:

Peptic ulcer disease

Esophagitis

GERD

Prevention of NSAIDs induced PUD

Zollinger Ellison syndrome

In H. Pylori triple therapy

Off label uses include in patients on antiplatelet therapy before or after endoscopy procedure (high risk for bleeding)

Pharmacokinetics

They are available as oral and IV formulations, and they are best administered before food intake

PPIs are prodrugs, they are activated after undergoing an acid catalyzed cleavage in the acidic secretory canaliculi of the parietal cells in the stomach

PPIs are metabolized by hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme, higher blood levels in patients from Asian ethnicities and in elderly patients

Adverse effects

Common adverse effects include: headache, nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain, fatigue and dizziness

Infrequent adverse effects include: rash, constipation, anxiety, depression and myopathies

Rarely it may lead to hypomagnesemia, in this case magnesium level can’t be replenished by supplementation so PPIs has to be discontinued; hypomagnesemia present as tetany, seizure, muscle weakness, delirium and cardiac arrhythmias

Infection: acidic environment act as a chemical barrier against bacterial infections, PPIs suppress acid secretion leading to increased risk of C difficile infections, other enteric infections and CAP

Rebound acid secretion: prolonged acid suppression lead to increased levels of gastrin and histamine which when the PPIs are discontinued, they act to increase acid secretion to levels higher than before initiation of PPIs treatment

Vit B12 deficiency with prolonged use: due to interference with IF secretion by the stomach (it needs acidic environment to be secreted)

Iron, calcium, magnesium deficiencies all due to lack of acid (because acid is important for breakdown of foods and release of micronutrients)

Monitoring

On prolonged use, Magnesium level and vit B12 level have to be monitored
